decisions.reason: Dependent type and original identity are confirmed: in Experiment 2, the authors collect new online webcam eye-tracking data (N = 90 native English speakers) to re-test the monolingual English visual world experiment of Dijkgraaf, Hartsuiker, and Duyck (2017, published online 2016; DOI 10.1017/S1366728916000547), using a re-analysis of Dijkgraaf et al.'s original lab dataset as a comparison baseline (while Experiment 1 is a general non-linguistic fixation calibration task rather than a re-test of a specific published empirical finding). For outcome, the authors explicitly state an overall replication verdict that Experiment 2 replicated the overall effect and pattern of Dijkgraaf et al. (2017): participants fixated significantly more on the target object picture in the semantically constraining verb condition than in the neutral condition (cluster permutation p < 0.05; logit mixed-effect model beta = 0.164, z = 3.983, p < 0.001). Under the codebook, an explicit overall replication verdict governs, and neither the smaller online effect size (roughly 60% of the in-lab effect) nor the ~200 ms technical measurement latency in WebGazer.js (attributed to browser/webcam processing and participant variance) negates the successful verdict. Both the shipped record and blind coding correctly coded 'successful'.
